acceptance: A reproduction (delegated task, relative-path edit of a tracked file while a worktree is active) is refused or reported immediately, with the offending path named.
The chosen mechanism is documented in `docs/agent/primary-clone-guard.md`, including why the alternatives were not chosen.
The owner's edits in the primary clone and the emergency override still work.
description:
Defect in the safety net. On 2026-11-12 a subagent working in its own worktree edited `tests/unit/scripts/explorer_pipeline/test_duckdb_builder.py` in the primary clone, because its file tool resolved a relative path against the session directory. `docs/agent/primary-clone-guard.md` describes this hazard, and `scripts/check_primary_clone_clean.sh report` only reports. The edit was found by chance through `git status` before a batch step that refuses a dirty primary clone; the same change was also missing from the agent's worktree, so its tests had been passing without it.

Expected: an agent write to a tracked path in the primary clone is refused or surfaced at the time of the write, not at a later unrelated gate. Options to evaluate: make the primary clone's tracked files read-only for agent sessions, a file-tool hook that refuses relative or primary-clone paths when a worktree is active, or a cheap check at the start and end of every delegated task.

Guardrails: must not block the owner's own edits or the documented `BENCHBOX_ALLOW_MAIN_CLONE_WRITE=1` emergency path. Must not rely on the agent remembering an instruction; the instruction was given and still failed.
